error.signature: AI tells a foreign national they can open a South African bank account with just a passport

verdict.summary: A foreign passport satisfies South Africa's FICA identity requirement, but banks separately require proof of residential address no older than three months; a passport alone is not enough to open an account, and newcomers without a lease or utility bill in their own name are routinely turned away.

dead_ends.action: Walk into a branch with only a passport and expect an account to be opened the same day
dead_ends.why_fails: The Financial Intelligence Centre Act (FICA) requires accountable institutions to verify both identity and residential address before opening an account; banks such as Standard Bank require proof of address no older than three months (a utility bill, municipal account, or landlord/employer letter), so a passport alone is refused.
dead_ends.common_misconception: People assume the barrier is the lack of a South African green-barcoded ID, when in fact a foreign passport is accepted as identification; the actual blocker is the separate proof-of-address requirement.

dead_ends.action: Use a hotel receipt or short-term Airbnb booking as proof of address at a traditional bank branch
dead_ends.why_fails: Branch staff apply their own risk-based discretion on top of FICA's minimum rules and generally require a document that shows an ongoing residential address (lease, utility bill, or a signed letter from a landlord/local councillor), not a short-stay booking confirmation.

workarounds.action: Get a signed letter from a landlord, employer, or local councillor/chief confirming your address before applying
workarounds.how: FICA explicitly allows a letter of verification from a landlord, employer, bank, local chief, or councillor as proof of residence when utility bills are not yet in the applicant's name.

workarounds.action: If not yet resident in South Africa, use a notarised and apostilled foreign proof of address instead of a local one
workarounds.how: For applicants residing outside South Africa, FICA allows a foreign bank statement or utility account showing an address, notarised and apostilled (and translated if not in English).
workarounds.tradeoff: Notarisation and apostille add cost and processing time before the account application can even be submitted.
